tools.name: get_catalog
tools.description: List what can be printed: SKUs (storybook books, sticker-a3 wall charts, greeting-card-a5 folded cards), formats, supported trim sizes, page-count limits, prices (INR, shipping included), and shipping coverage (India only). Call this first to quote a price or check whether a PDF will be accepted.

tools.name: create_upload
tools.description: Start a PDF upload. Returns {upload_id, put_url, expires_at, max_bytes}. HTTP PUT the raw PDF bytes to put_url (Content-Type: application/pdf, no auth needed — the URL is signed). The PUT response includes the validation report. Then pass upload_id to create_order. Keyless use is bounded per calling

tools.name: validate_pdf
tools.description: Get the print-validation report for an uploaded PDF before paying: page count, trim size, hard errors (blocking) and soft warnings (non-blocking). Every error includes a `resolution` explaining how to fix it. Free to call; use it to check printability before create_order.

tools.name: create_order
tools.description: Create a print order for a validated upload. Validates everything BEFORE any payment link is minted. Returns { order, order_token } — the order object has order_id, status, amount, and payment_url (the Razorpay link, present while awaiting_payment). findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_upload · Private data: create_upload, get_order, cancel_order, apply_enterprise · Public sink: create_upload, create_order.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_upload · Private data: create_upload, get_order, cancel_order, apply_enterprise · Public sink: create_upload, create_order

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_order" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
